penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Salesforce permission gap analysis for enterprise clients requires understanding each client's specific org configuration, security policies, and compliance requirements — this is inherently per-client consulting work that cannot be fully automated by Claude without hands-on access to each Salesforce org.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Selling governance/compliance tooling to enterprise Salesforce accounts reliably requires discovery calls and solution scoping; the consultant posting this is already working in a synchronous client-service model.

rationale: The buyer — Salesforce consultants and enterprise admins — is identifiable and has budget, but the problem (granular permission gaps in Salesforce) is highly org-specific, Salesforce platform-dependent, and the kind of issue that gets resolved either by Salesforce's own roadmap or by paid consultants doing bespoke configuration work. Delivering a genuinely useful automated solution would require per-org org access and nuanced configuration judgment, making this a consulting engagement, not an autonomous micro-service. The total drops to 2.5 after penalties, well below any threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended to pursue as an autonomous factory service. The problem requires per-client Salesforce org access to diagnose and remediate permission gaps — there is no standardized deliverable Claude can generate that would be useful without knowing each client's specific configuration. This is fundamentally a consulting engagement that a Salesforce-certified admin or ISV consultant delivers in billable hours. A non-technical solo operator without Salesforce domain expertise (founder_fit=3) cannot build or sell into this space competitively.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (scored 4, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai_min (scored 5, floor is 6). Total after penalties is 2.5, well below min_total_to_validate (5.5). Drop.
